logline: A deaf prince dismissed by his entire kingdom as too small and powerless to rule sets out to become the greatest king in the world, discovering that the ranking system everyone obeys conceals something far darker than court politics.

renewal.note: The main 23-episode series aired October 2021 to March 2022. A spin-off, Ranking of Kings: The Treasure Chest of Courage, aired 10 episodes in April-June 2023. The source manga by Sosuke Toka went on hiatus in April 2023 and resumed December 2024.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb holds at 8.4 and MAL users score it 8.49, reflecting a strong consensus from a large viewing base. Rotten Tomatoes shows 90 percent from 1 critic review; Slashfilm praised its emotionally complex characters. AniTrendz scored it 77/100, noting pacing unevenness in the second half.

pull_quotes.text: Characters initially appear simplistic but are revealed to be emotionally complex and fully-fledged.

seasons.review_body: Ranking of Kings aired on Fuji TV's Noitamina block from October 2021 to March 2022, produced by Wit Studio from Sosuke Toka's web manga. The premise - a deaf, physically diminutive prince seeking the world's highest rank - positioned itself as a subversive take on fantasy tropes, and critics broadly accepted that framing. Slashfilm noted characters initially appear simplistic but become emotionally complex. IMDb users landed at 8.4; MAL registers 8.49. AniTrendz's 77/100 review identified a structural split: the first half, built on Bojji's underdog arc, was praised for excellent pacing; the second half's escalating revelations divided opinion. The presence of a deaf protagonist in a high-fantasy setting drew notice across anime criticism as a meaningful design choice. The series streams internationally on Amazon Prime Video and Funimation.

episode_reviews.title: The New King
episode_reviews.review_body: Ranking of Kings Season 1 Episode 1 'The New King' aired October 15, 2021 on Fuji TV's Noitamina block as the premiere of Wit Studio's 23-episode series. IMDb users scored the series 8.4 and MyAnimeList users 8.49 from a large base. Slashfilm noted that characters initially appear simplistic but are revealed to be emotionally complex. The premiere introduces Bojji, a deaf prince physically dismissed by his entire court, subjected to a series of humiliations that a lesser series would use as straightforward underdog setup. What distinguishes the episode is the speed with which it complicates that framing: Bojji's genuine warmth and the unexpected appearance of the shadow creature Kage establish a bond that will carry the series. The episode earned an individual IMDb rating of 8.8, the series' highest for any single hour, reflecting viewer consensus that the premiere executed the concept with immediate emotional clarity.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere introduces Bojji through a series of humiliations that would crush a lesser protagonist, then immediately reveals the depth beneath the surface with a single wordless sequence. The episode earned an individual IMDb rating of 8.8, the series' highest for any single hour.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bojji's first genuine smile - and what the shadow Kage makes of it.

episode_reviews.title: The Gigan Clan and the Greatest King
episode_reviews.review_body: Ranking of Kings Season 1 Episode 23 'The Gigan Clan and the Greatest King' aired March 25, 2022 on Fuji TV as the finale of Wit Studio's 23-episode series. IMDb holds the series at 8.4; MAL users scored it 8.49. Slashfilm praised characters who appear simplistic but prove emotionally complex. The finale delivers the payoff of Bojji's arc across both its emotional and action registers: the coming-of-age question the series posed in its premiere - what constitutes a great king when conventional measures exclude you from consideration - receives an answer the show has earned through consistent investment in both its protagonist and ensemble. AniTrendz's 77/100 season review identified pacing issues in the second half, a fair critique: the final revelations carry accumulated lore weight that some critics felt diluted the first half's cleaner storytelling. The emotional catharsis, however, holds.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the season's central arc and delivers an emotional catharsis that cuts through the show's fairy-tale register. The ending can land differently for those who feel the second half over-complicates what the first half sets up cleanly.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bojji's final declaration of intent - the moment the premise of the entire series earns its payoff.
